# Reducing Crane Downtime with IoT

Amadeo Ibbwick: Welcome back to The Brilet Sessions, everyone. Today, we’re diving into a critical topic—how IoT tech is cutting crane downtime at maritime ports. Jessamy Silvmoor, PortTech Innovations’ lead engineer, joins us. Jessamy, what was the turning point that made you champion telemetry sensors on cranes?

Jessamy Silvmoor: Thanks, Amadeo. It was actually last summer at Southgate Port. We had a massive backlog—over 300 containers delayed because one crane’s gearbox failed unexpectedly. That sparked the idea: what if the crane could tell us it was struggling before breaking down?

Amadeo: Makes sense. So, how did IoT sensors change the game?

Jessamy: We installed vibration and temperature sensors on all twenty cranes. The system flags anomalies in real time. For example, last month, one crane showed abnormal heat spikes in a motor bearing. The maintenance team was dispatched immediately—no downtime, no backlog.

Amadeo: Impressive. Has this improved overall port efficiency?

Jessamy: Absolutely. Crane downtime has dropped by 40% in six months, saving the port roughly $500,000 monthly in operational costs.

Amadeo: Incredible impact. Thanks for sharing, Jessamy.
